# Selective bloom

Bloom from selected objects only: give it a selection or texture mask and just those pixels feed the glow, which still spreads over everything around them. Without a mask it is ordinary bloom.

<EffectDemo effect="selective-bloom" />

## Usage

```ts
import { EffectComposer } from '@mk7s/xtree/core';
import { selectiveBloom } from '@mk7s/xtree/effects/selective-bloom';

const composer = new EffectComposer(renderer);
composer.setScene(scene, camera);
const hero = scene.getObjectByName('hero'); // the objects to select
composer.add(selectiveBloom({ mask: { selection: [hero] } }));
renderer.setAnimationLoop(() => composer.render());
```

Every parameter is also a property: `effect.intensity = 1`. Uniform changes take effect on the next frame without recompiling.

## Parameters

| Parameter   | Type                                                      | Default     | Range | Description                                                                              |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `intensity` | number                                                    | `1`         | 0 – 4 | How much of the blurred light is added back.                                             |
| `threshold` | number                                                    | `1`         | 0 – 8 | Linear brightness above which pixels bloom. 1 is the brightest non-HDR white.            |
| `knee`      | number                                                    | `0.5`       | 0 – 1 | Softness of the threshold, as a fraction of it.                                          |
| `radius`    | number                                                    | `0.7`       | 0 – 1 | Spread: low values keep the glow tight, high values favor the widest blur levels.        |
| `levels`    | integer                                                   | `6`         | 2 – 8 | Number of half-resolution blur levels. More levels reach further and cost a little more. |
| `tint`      | hex color (theme: [`accent`](/guide/holocss#theme-roles)) | `'#ffffff'` |       | Color multiplied into the glow.                                                          |
| `luminance` | 'threshold' \| 'all'                                      | `'all'`     |       | Masked pixels bloom above the threshold, or all of them whatever their brightness.       |

Every effect also has `blend` (any of the 26 [blend modes](/reference/shaders#modes)), `opacity` (0–1) and `enabled`.

## Presets

| Preset     | Settings                                                     |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `neon`     | `intensity: 2`, `radius: 0.55`, `knee: 0.2`                  |
| `halo`     | `intensity: 1.2`, `radius: 0.9`, `levels: 8`                 |
| `hotspots` | `luminance: 'threshold'`, `threshold: 0.8`, `intensity: 1.5` |
| `tinted`   | `tint: '#7cc4ff'`, `intensity: 1.6`                          |

Apply one with `selectiveBloom({ preset: 'name' })` or `effect.applyPreset('name')`; presets start from the defaults.

## Details

- **Family:** Blur & glow · tracked as story X5.3 in the [plan](https://github.com/s4njee/xtree/blob/main/plan.md).
- **Passes:** samples the pass input at other positions, so it starts a new merged pass; following pixel effects join that pass. It also renders its own intermediate passes before the merged pass.
- **Masks:** reads its `mask` itself rather than fading by it (see the description); any [mask kind](/guide/masks) works.
- **Motion:** Static: nothing animates.
- **Size:** 7.1 KB gzip budget for `@mk7s/xtree/effects/selective-bloom`, including the shared effect runtime.

### Selecting what glows

```ts
const glowing = selectiveBloom({ intensity: 1.5 });
glowing.mask = { selection: [sign, lamp] }; // or { selection: { layer: 2 } }
```

The selection is rendered to a mask each frame, so objects in front still hide the selected ones; with `xray: true` they bloom through. Texture masks also work. Depth masks don't limit the bloom source; use a selection or texture instead.
